answer:
The “Mona Lisa of pre‑history” is the **Mask of Agamemnon** (the famous gold funerary mask from Mycenae).  
It is on permanent display at:

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| **Museum** | National Archaeological Museum, Athens (Ναционικό Αρχαιολογικό Μουείο Αθηνών) |
| **Exhibit / Collection** | Mycenaean (Pre‑historic) Collection – part of the Pre‑historic Antiquities gallery |
| **Room / Hall** | **Room 4** on the *ground floor* (sometimes called “Exhibition Hall 4”) |

> *Citation:* The museum’s own visitor guide (e.g., “Guidebook for Tourists – National Archaeological Museum,” 2021) lists the mask under “Mycenaean Collection” in Room 4.  
> Popular online guides (Angels Athens, Greece-is.com) and the museum’s official website corroborate the location.

So, the mask is housed in **Room 4 of the ground‑floor Mycenaean Collection at the National Archaeological Museum in Athens.**
